review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its simp-related declarations: the `attribute [-simp]` line, the `@[scoped simp]` lemmas, the rfl and Iff.rfl API lemmas, and the explicit `rw`/`simp only` chains. I also read the upstream definitions of `LocalGL2.swapUnit_val`, `scalarGL_coe`, `diagSnd_coe` and `unitOfNeZero_coe`, and Mathlib's `mem_adicCompletionIntegers`. I did not run Lean. I did not report `coe_piK`/`coe_piO` (scoped simp, rfl, harmless) or the unused rfl lemmas `coe_ψ` and `coe_units_map_ev`, because Mathlib's `Units.coe_map` already covers the unit-coercion cases. Both findings are modest. The first depends on why `swapUnit_val` was disabled, which the file does not say. The second is a convenience improvement, not a correctness problem.

findings.problem: This file never mentions `swapUnit`, yet it has to switch off an upstream `@[simp]` lemma to keep its own simp calls working. The same `LocalGL2.swapUnit_val` removal is copied into many other files (e.g. the Pic0 theorem files). That pattern suggests the lemma is a globally unwanted simp rule: it expands `↑swapUnit` into an explicit matrix literal whenever GL(2) matrices are simplified. Each downstream file must discover and patch this separately, which hides the real simp-interface issue.
findings.proposed_change: Fix the simp interface at the source. In `Definitions/Def_LocalLanglands_CartanDecomposition.lean` (line 111), drop `@[simp]` from `swapUnit_val`, or make it `@[scoped simp]`, or restrict it to the files that need the explicit-matrix form. Then delete this `attribute [-simp]` workaround line from this file and its copies. If a downstream simp call really needs the unfolding, state it with `simp [LocalGL2.swapUnit_val]` at that call.
findings.benefit: Downstream files, including this one, get a clean default simp set without a per-file opt-out. It also avoids accidental expansion of `swapUnit` coercions into matrix literals in unrelated GL(2) proofs.

findings.problem: `mem_intMat_iff` and `mem_K0_iff` are `Iff.rfl` unfolding lemmas for the bundled `intMat` and `K0`, but they are not simp lemmas. Every use is therefore a hand-ordered `rw` chain. `ψ_mem_K0_iff` repeats `mem_intMat_iff`, `SetLike.mem_coe` and `hφR` twice, because `rw` rewrites only one instance per occurrence, and it then needs a closing `rfl` to match `ψ g⁻¹`. This is brittle: the chain depends on the order in which the membership goals appear, and it breaks if either side is restated. Any other membership goal for `intMat` or `K0` cannot be handled by `simp`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `mem_intMat_iff` and `mem_K0_iff` as `@[simp]`. The `intMat` carrier is a custom set, and the rewrite is non-looping, since the RHS contains only the `𝓞v` membership of entries. Then prove `ψ_mem_K0_iff` with `simp only [mem_K0_iff, mem_intMat_iff, Submodule.mem_localBoxUnits_iff, SetLike.mem_coe, hφR]`, or `simp [...]`. Keep the final `rfl` or `Units.val` bridge only if it is still needed.
findings.benefit: The membership unfolding is applied in all positions at once, so the double `rw` and its ordering dependence go away. Future lemmas about `K0` and `intMat` (e.g. `of_mem_intMat`-style goals) can use `simp` instead of a handcrafted rewrite chain.
